To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the seagull and sunset diagrams in a minimally coupled massless scalar theory in de Sitter contribute to the effective mass of the scalar field at the same order of the infrared enhancement, (b) trilinear interactions also contribute to the effective dynamical mass of the scalar, (c) the infrared divergencies of the two-point correlation function are self-regulated, and (d) this is true for both the seagull/sunset diagrams and the trilinear interactions

(i) the self-energy of a massless scalar field in de-Sitter space is finite at one-loop, (ii) this self-energy is non-zero and is proportional to the Hubble parameter squared, and (iii) this self-energy induces a dynamical mass that self-regulates the infrared divergencies of the scalar two-point correlation function in the infrared.
